In 2 months since my previous comment, I think this issue has been the main thing preventing me from using OpenCode desktop. 

File editing is such a basic, necessary feature that I am baffled anyone thought it would be okay to ship an IDE without it. 

It's not "next-level thinking for an emerging no-code world", it's just bad UX to type 2 lines of text to make a potentially 3 character edit which will be applied non-deterministically and costs me money.

Confirming this on a purely local setup — no remote server involved — and adding the code path that causes it.

**Environment:** opencode 1.17.18, macOS arm64, server started locally (`opencode serve`).

**Reproduction:** renamed a local git repo directory,
`~/Desktop/git/opencode-memex` → `~/Desktop/git/opencode-codex-memory`.
Afterwards every client keeps presenting the project under the dead old path. Clearing client-side state (`opencode.global.dat:server`, workspace keys, session/local storage) does not help — the client re-learns the dead path from the server on the next connect, exactly as described above.

**DB state in `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`:**

```
id       = c7d111b3…            (git-derived project id)
worktree = /Users/…/opencode-memex          <- dead path, still displayed
sandboxes = ["/Users/…/opencode-codex-memory"]  <- renamed dir demoted to a sandbox
```

**Why it happens** — `Project.fromDirectory` in `packages/opencode/src/project/project.ts` (current main): the project id is git-derived, so the renamed directory resolves to the existing project row, and the upsert deliberately keeps the old worktree for non-global projects:

```ts
const result: Info = {
  ...existing,
  worktree: projectID === ProjectV2.ID.global ? worktree : existing.worktree,
  ...
}
```

The directory being opened is then merely appended to `sandboxes` because it differs from the (stale) worktree:

```ts
if (
  projectID !== ProjectV2.ID.global &&
  data.directory !== result.worktree &&
  !result.sandboxes.includes(data.directory)
)
  result.sandboxes.push(data.directory)
```

Notably, `sandboxes` are filtered through `fs.exists` right below — but the worktree itself is never validated. So a dead worktree is re-persisted verbatim on every access, forever.

**Workaround confirmed:** stopping the server and repointing `project.worktree` (plus `session.directory` / `session.path` for old sessions) in `opencode.db` fixes it fully.

A fix along the lines of the issue's "Expected" seems natural given the code above: when `existing.worktree` no longer exists and `data.directory` resolves to the same project, adopt `data.directory` as the new worktree (i.e. apply the same existence check to the worktree that `sandboxes` already get).
I resolved the issue by reinstalling Opencode GUI on Windows. It's working fine now. I'm closing the ticket.

Hey! Your PR title `Vm main` doesn't follow conventional commit format.

### Use case: Compositional bash approval to reduce permission prompts

When an agent uses compound bash commands like `echo "label" && ls .claude/skills/ | head -20`, each chained/piped invocation triggers a separate `bash: ask` permission prompt. Even when every atomic command in the chain would individually pass the permission rules (all paths within the workspace), the compound command as a whole requires user approval.

**What a PreToolUse hook could do:**

1. Tokenize the compound bash command into individual commands (split on `&&`, `|`, `;`)
2. Check each atomic command against the existing allow/deny rules as if run standalone
3. Trace pipe boundaries — if a pipe sends data from an allowed command to one that writes outside the sandbox, still require approval
4. Auto-approve when every leaf command passes individually and no cross-boundary data flow exists

This would eliminate unnecessary approval prompts for routine verification workflows (checking diffs, listing files, verifying grep output) while still blocking genuinely risky compositions.

**Current workaround:** Agents avoid compound commands by using single-purpose `bash` calls and the dedicated file-operation tools (`grep`, `glob`, `read`) instead of `rg`/`ls`/`cat` in bash. This works but forces verbose, fragmented agent behavior.

Thanks for the detailed report. We confirmed this behavior in the current V1 implementation.

The reported failure is resolved in OpenCode V2, which we're planning to release soon. The V2 work is available on the [`v2` branch](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/tree/v2).

V2's explicit MCP authorization path no longer decides whether OAuth is required from the `initialize` response. It invokes the MCP SDK's authorization flow directly:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/d88faeb6da973434410af2873e467035427e654c/packages/core/src/mcp/oauth.ts#L212-L215

The SDK then performs RFC 9728 protected-resource discovery independently of `initialize`, including the standard path-aware metadata location:

https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/blob/v1.29.0/src/client/auth.ts#L488-L499

V2 also supplies that OAuth provider to the streamable HTTP transport:

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/d88faeb6da973434410af2873e467035427e654c/packages/core/src/mcp/client.ts#L204-L209

The transport recognizes a later `401`, extracts `resource_metadata` and scope from `WWW-Authenticate`, and enters the SDK's authorization/refresh logic:

https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/blob/v1.29.0/src/client/streamableHttp.ts#L489-L518

We verified the reported server shape against V2: `initialize` and `tools/list` returned `200`, while `tools/call` returned `401`. V2 discovered the protected-resource metadata and produced the OAuth authorization URL. Unlike V1, invoking MCP authorization does not falsely report success without storing credentials.

### Try the V2 beta

V2 is currently a work in progress. Beta data may be wiped, features may break, and APIs and configuration may continue to change. You can install it alongside V1 from npm's `next` tag:

```sh
npm install -g @opencode-ai/cli@next
```

The beta installs as a separate executable:

```sh
opencode2
```

See the [V2 beta documentation](https://v2.opencode.ai/) for current setup and migration details.
